sources: Penn State Extension, Cellar Spiders (S. Jacobs): family Pholcidae, often called daddy longlegs; very long thin legs, small body; live in dark damp places such as basements and crawl spaces; loose irregular webs in corners; when disturbed they vibrate rapidly in the web; feed on insects and other spiders; harmless to people; https://extension.psu.edu/cellar-spiders

UC Riverside, Spider Research (R. Vetter), The 'Daddy-long-legs Spider is the Most Venomous Spider' Myth: no evidence pholcid venom is dangerous to people; the 'fangs too short' claim is false; https://spiders.ucr.edu/daddy-long-legs-myth

Burke Museum, Spider Myths (R. Crawford): cellar spiders are a major predator of other spiders, invading webs; females carry their eggs in their jaws; https://www.burkemuseum.org/collections-and-research/biology/arachnology-and-entomology/spider-myths
MythBusters episode 13 (2004): Adam Savage let a daddy-longlegs spider bite him and felt only a brief mild burning sensation.

beats.say: Number seventeen. The cellar spider. Most people call it a daddy longlegs.
Tiny body, eight super long legs, in a messy web up in the corner of your basement.
The myth says its venom is the deadliest of all, but its fangs are too short to bite you.
Wrong, twice. A MythBusters host let one bite him. He felt a tiny burn. That's it.
And it hunts other spiders. It walks into their webs, and eats the owner.
Daddy longlegs. F tier. Harmless to you. Myth busted.
